title: Flowering phenology and female fitness: Impact of a pre-dispersal seed predator on a sexually polymorphic species
screening_reason: Direct plant seasonal timing, Hadena predation and final unattacked mature-seed fruit production are measured, but no independently quantified moth-activity curve supports strict synchrony.
notes: Dianthus sylvestris × Hadena compta; two annual relative-fitness slopes extracted to timing-sensitivity lane.

title: Do Flower Color and Floral Scent of Silene Species affect Host Preference of Hadena bicruris a Seed-Eating Pollinator under Field Conditions?
screening_reason: Flowering status and seed predation are scored, but the focal analysis is host preference/seed attack and lacks the strict timing-to-final-fitness estimand.

title: The contribution of a pollinating seed predator to selection on Silene latifolia females
screening_reason: Hadena attack and female reproductive traits permit selection decomposition, but plant-partner temporal matching is not the exposure.

title: Impact of Flowering Phenology of Silene alba and S. dioica on Susceptibility to Fungal Infection and Seed Predation
screening_reason: Anthesis timing, fruit set, fruit predation and undamaged fruits per flower are measured in the same field populations, but the moth-activity distribution is not independently quantified as a strict synchrony exposure and anther-smut is an additional interacting agent.
notes: Biere & Honders 1996. Early S. dioica and late S. alba differed in undamaged-fruit success through different fruit-set/predation pathways; strong timing-sensitivity evidence.

title: Importance of Silene latifolia ssp. alba and S. dioica as host plants of the parasitic pollinator Hadena bicruris
screening_reason: Plant flowering periods and Hadena oviposition/activity periods are directly compared, but plant final reproductive fitness is not the endpoint needed for H1.
notes: Bopp & Gottsberger 2004. Valuable complement to IWE044 because it measures the partner timing that IWE044 lacks.

title: Direct and indirect effects of pollinators and seed predators to selection on plant and floral traits
screening_reason: Pollination and predispersal seed-predation pathways to female fitness are quantified, but the study concerns floral/plant traits rather than temporal matching to partner activity.
notes: Castilleja linariaefolia; strong multi-agent mechanism context.

title: Effects of experimental manipulation of inflorescence size on pollination and pre-dispersal seed predation in Ipomopsis aggregata
screening_reason: Pollinator visitation, seed predation and female reproductive success are experimentally linked, but the manipulated axis is inflorescence size rather than timing.
notes: Brody & Mitchell 1997; retain as linked pollinator-antagonist design context, not timing evidence.

title: Does seed production of spring ephemerals decrease when spring comes early?
screening_reason: An exceptionally early spring shifted flowering and reduced seed set in bee-pollinated species while two fly-pollinated species were unaffected, but partner emergence/activity was not quantified sufficiently for the strict synchrony estimand.
notes: Kudo et al. 2004; precursor to the later Corydalis direct-mismatch programme and potentially dependent historical context for IWE001/IWE002.
